title: Redwood PLG Quickstart Discovery - Nebula Systems
summary: Intro discovery for PLG/self-serve Redwood API quickstart. Customer wants to evaluate hosted API for fastest time-to-first-token, understand free credits and quickstart flow. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private for compliance and latency/cost tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: provision trial org with credits, share SOC2/KMS docs, schedule technical deep-dive and benchmark run with sample payloads.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-08-04 | Time: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 42 minutes | Location: Zoom | Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO - Nebula), Ben Ortiz (Head of ML - Nebula), Sam Park (SRE - Nebula)
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options
action_items: Jordan Miles: Send trial invite + quickstart guide + free credits details (due: 2026-08-06)
Priya Rao: Schedule technical deep-dive and benchmarking session (due: 2026-08-10)
Aisha Khan: Share sample workload and expected QPS/latency targets (due: 2026-08-07)
Sam Park: Provide network/security contacts for VPC discussion (due: 2026-08-07)
next_steps: Jordan to create trial org and allocate free credits
Redwood SE to run a micro-benchmark with customer's sample payloads
Schedule technical deep-dive (1 hour) week of Aug 10
Send SOC2 and KMS integration docs and network checklist
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to chat through Redwood's PLG quickstart, i'll do a short intro and then priya will cover tech details. 
[00:07] Aisha: thanks Jordan, yeah we just want to see how fast we can get to first token — basically demo and maybe run some small bench marks, and then figure out if we go hosted to start or we need dedicated for compliance. 
[00:18] Ben: yeah hi i'm Ben, head of ML — key things for us are latency under 200ms p50 for short prompts, cost per 1k tokens, and how easy it is to spin up. we also care about data residency, audit logs. 
[00:29] Priya: great — quick note on naming, sometimes folks see "Redwood Dedicated" or "Redwood Private" — we have three modes: hosted API (fastest to value), Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem). 
[00:41] Sam: ah ok, yeah for us security is big, we're regulated so VPC and KMS is likely required later. for the quickstart though, we just want to poke at the hosted flow. 
[00:50] Jordan: perfect, our PLG quickstart is designed for that — sign up, get free credits, follow a quickstart that takes you from signup to first token in like 10-15 minutes. there's an SDK and curl examples. 
[01:02] Aisha: what's in the free credits? is it time-limited or usage-limited? 
[01:06] Jordan: it's usage-limited, typically $X00 in credits for evaluation, expires after 30 days. we'll include sample prompts and a benchmark notebook. 
[01:15] Ben: oh nice. on latency, you mentioned 200ms p50 — is that realistic on hosted for small prompts? 
[01:21] Priya: depends on model & prompt length. for shorter instruct models on our hosted infra, p50 can be ~100-150ms for 32-64 tokens. public clouds and model size matter — we can share profiles. sometimes latency numbers vary because of kv cache warmup and batching. 
[01:36] Ben: kv cash? did you say KV cash — k-v cache — got it. 
[01:40] Jordan: yeah i hear that a lot, the autos transcriber turned it into cash the other day. 
[01:45] Aisha: ha. ok can you outline the steps to get us running? and what are the obvious blockers? 
[01:50] Jordan: step one: sign up for the trial link — i'll send it. step two: follow quickstart to create an API key and run sample requests. step three: we can run a micro-benchmark with your payloads — priya will help. blockers: if you need VPC private deployment, that's a bigger project — but you can still start on hosted for function dev and then move to dedicated/private later. 
[02:08] Sam: for VPC, does Redwood support customer-managed KMS? 
[02:12] Priya: yes, for Private we support KMS/HSM integrations, and for Dedicated we have options too. we'll send the KMS integration doc. 
[02:20] Ben: on compliance, do you have SOC 2 and iso certs? 
[02:23] Jordan: yes SOC 2 Type II, and our security pack includes audit logs, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC. i'll attach the SOC2 summary and the security checklist. 
[02:33] Aisha: great — also interested in data retention policies and delete APIs. 
[02:37] Priya: we have retention controls and delete APIs, plus per-customer retention defaults. we'll share the policy doc. 
[02:42] Ben: moving to dedicated — if we hit the latency/cost envelope is it straightforward to move? like can we pin a model version and keep the same API surface? 
[02:51] Priya: yes that's a core part of our platform — same API and SDK across hosted, dedicated, and private. you can pin model versions and rollout canary traffic. the main work is capacity planning and commit sizing for dedicated. 
[03:05] Sam: commit sizing — do you have an example for throughput vs GPU types? 
[03:09] Priya: yes we have benchmark profiles per GPU type and model; for example 1xA10 can handle X rps for small chat payloads, and we provide tuning tips — we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet. 
[03:19] Ben: you mentioned automatic fallback to compatible model variants — can you explain? 
[03:23] Jordan: if you set routing policies, when Dedicated is saturated we can failover to hosted variants or lower-cost quantized models to maintain availability. this helps reliability during spikes. 
[03:34] Aisha: that's interesting; we have unpredictable spikes in customer support traffic, so graceful degradation matters. 
[03:39] Ben: what's the expected unit cost delta between hosted and dedicated? ballpark. 
[03:43] Jordan: ballpark — hosted can be higher per-token but no commit; dedicated reduces unit cost with reserved capacity. depends on utilization. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations on batching and quantization to lower costs. 
[03:55] Sam: do you support streaming responses and function calling? our pipelines need streaming. 
[03:59] Priya: yes streaming, function/tool calling, structured outputs are supported on hosted and Dedicated; Private supports the same features but requires some network config. 
[04:08] Ben: ok real quick on quickstart: how long from signup to first token realistically? 
[04:12] Jordan: most teams are first token in 10-20 minutes if they follow the quickstart. sometimes SSO or corporate firewall rules add time. 
[04:20] Aisha: perfect — we'll try that today. can you include a short checklist for network and firewall rules for the trial? 
[04:26] Priya: yes we have a network checklist for corporate firewalls; for the hosted quickstart you only need outbound HTTPS to our API endpoints. for Private you'll need VPC peering or PrivateLink. 
[04:36] Ben: what about logging and tracing — can we get token-level cost breakdown for our routes? 
[04:41] Jordan: yes Redwood Console has token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards and traces. we'll give you access to a demo console. 
[04:50] Sam: any rate limits for trial orgs? we sometimes run synthetic loads. 
[04:54] Jordan: trial orgs have soft limits to protect shared infra; we can increase for benchmark runs if coordinated with our SEs. 
[05:01] Aisha: timeline-wise, if we like the trial what's a typical pilot -> dedicated timeline? 
[05:06] Priya: pilots are often 4-8 weeks for a focused PoC. dedicated onboarding can take a few weeks more for capacity and networking. 
[05:14] Ben: ok can we scope a PoC — we want 2 models: a short chat model for customer support and an embeddings flow for semantic search. 
[05:22] Jordan: that sounds standard — quickstart for the chat model on hosted, and embeddings pipeline can be tested with our embeddings endpoint. we should get your sample corpus to size embeddings throughput. 
[05:33] Priya: action items: we'll run a micro-benchmark with your short-chat payloads and 1k-document embeddings test. Jordan will provision trial credits. 
[05:43] Aisha: thanks. last Q: do you have any public perf benchmarks we can look at? 
[05:47] Jordan: yes we maintain a model catalog with perf profiles; i'll share the link and a benchmarking spreadsheet. 
[05:55] Ben: great, thanks everyone. 
[05:57] Jordan: thanks all — to recap, jordan to send trial + quickstart, priya to schedule bench and deep dive, customer to share payloads and network contacts. we'll follow up by email with links and docs. 
[06:10] Aisha: thanks, bye. 
[06:12] Ben: bye. 
[06:13] Sam: bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional transcription artefacts (KV cash / kv cache), filler words preserved, some speaker overlap.
